dossier.public_summary: The dip is on the target M dwarf but it is V-shaped, about an hour long, and has a second deep eclipse half an orbit later (about 60% as deep as the first). Together with a strong star-spot signal at about half the orbital period, this matches a grazing eclipsing stellar binary on the target, not a flat-bottomed planet transit.

reasons.why: Second dip near phase 0.5 is very deep (about half the primary depth) with high SNR, so primary+secondary together sum to ~100% modulation. A planet would need a circularized hot Jupiter with a tiny secondary, not a ~0.58 fraction. This is stellar eclipse behaviour with opposite inclination, plus phase_curve chi2 640.8 dof 9 amplitude 3122 ppm.
reasons.value: snr 92.02 at phase 0.4862 depth_ppm 30880 depth_over_dip 0.5832 best_brightening_snr 5.182

reasons.why: Strong V-shaped grazing eclipse and density mismatch (observed_h 0.7487 vs central_h 1.353 ratio 0.5533) favour a grazing stellar binary over a flat-bottomed planet transit, which would be bottom-flat at this SNR 147.7.
reasons.value: v_sigma 20.33 best_ingress_fraction 0.4 fit_b 0.7891 duration ratio 0.5533 fit_chi2_red 3.393 star_density_penalty 56.37

reasons.why: Depths are highly inconsistent with a planet on a spotted star. The rotation period is essentially half the 3.51-d signal, so the 'transit' period is at a 2x harmonic of a strong spot signal (8311-10193 ppm, false_alarm 4e-12-1e-18), favouring spots/binary modulation over a planetary orbit.
reasons.value: p_consistent 3.1426999430252875e-14 chi2 95.7 dof 14 outliers depth 61092 sigma 4.8 rotation_d 1.76 signal_over_rotation 1.9969 amplitude_ppm 8311-10193

reasons.why: The dip is securely on the target (all neighbours >68 sigma away) and sector-depth scatter is calibration between SPOC 2-min (50715 ppm) and TESS-SPOC (53441, 54309 ppm), ruling out a neighbour blend. The remaining on-target signal is therefore intrinsic to the star: eclipsing binary, not a planet, as also shown by odd_even diff_sigma 0.2676 and xgboost planet_rank 0.12.
